ANALYSIS COMPLETE (script: build_analysis.py, output: analysis_output.txt). All three guardrails applied.

SAMPLE
- Full sample 12,686. Complete-case modeling set (all vars): n=3,717; baseline-set-only complete case: n=8,467. Selection note: complete-casing on the 1981 academic variables (class rank 55% missing) shrinks the set ~70% and may select for continued schooling/engagement; results are associations within this subset.
- 16+ outcome cell: 37 in full sample, 26 in baseline set, only 17 in the modeling set — degenerate, as flagged.

OLS, CONTINUOUS grade1979 (n=3,717)
Baseline (race + SES), R²=0.051:
  black −0.0228 (p=.83) | hispanic −0.4098 (p<.001) | loginc79 −0.3366 (p<.001) | mothgrade +0.0749 (p<.001) | fathgrade +0.0445 (p<.001)
Augmented (+ asvab_comp, rank_pct), R²=0.069 (ΔR²=+0.019):
  black +0.0299 (p=.78) | hispanic −0.1831 (p=.04) | loginc79 −0.3444 (p<.001) | mothgrade +0.0588 (p<.001) | fathgrade +0.0263 (p=.02)
  asvab_comp +0.0028/pt (p<.001, ≈+0.28 grades per 100-pt SD) | rank_pct +0.4019 (p=.003)
Attenuation: hispanic −0.410 → −0.183 (55% shrink, still significant); black −0.023 → +0.030 (sign flip, both n.s.); loginc79 −0.337 → −0.344 (unchanged, −2%); mothgrade −22%; fathgrade −41%.

LOGIT / LPM, 16+ BINARY (n=3,717, 17 events — underpowered, directional only)
Logit baseline (pseudoR²=0.057): black +0.32 (p=.68), hispanic −1.12 (p=.28), loginc79 −0.18 (p=.28), mothgrade +0.12 (p=.34), fathgrade +0.15 (p=.11).
Logit augmented (pseudoR²=0.114): black +0.52 (p=.50), hispanic −0.29 (p=.79), loginc79 −0.20 (p=.21), mothgrade +0.05 (p=.68), fathgrade +0.08 (p=.39); asvab_comp +0.0108 (p=.03), rank_pct +1.20 (p=.35). Hispanic log-odds attenuate ~74% (−1.12 → −0.29).
LPM mirrors this: hispanic −0.0030 → +0.0003; asvab_comp p=.03.

DRAFT HYPOTHESIS (plain language, guardrails embedded)
"The dataset contains no explicit BA-completion or degree-earned variable; this analysis therefore uses the respondent's highest grade completed in 1979 as the education-attainment proxy, with a 16+ binary examined only as a degenerate sensitivity cell (37 cases in the full sample, 17 in the modeling set). In the complete-case modeling set (n=3,717), baseline models with race (Black, Hispanic vs non-Black/non-Hispanic) and pre-1979/1979 SES (log family income, mother's and father's grade) show a Hispanic gap of −0.41 grade (p<.001), a null Black coefficient (−0.02, n.s.), a negative family-income coefficient (−0.34, p<.001), and positive parental-education coefficients (+0.075 mother, +0.045 father per grade, both p<.001). Considering academic characteristics — the 1981 ASVAB composite (+0.0028 per point, p<.001) and class-rank percentile (+0.40, p=.003) — materially alters the picture: the Hispanic gap attenuates by about 55% (−0.41 → −0.18, still p=.04) and the Black coefficient flips sign (−0.02 → +0.03, both n.s.), parental-education coefficients shrink 20–40%, while the family-income coefficient is essentially unchanged (−0.34 → −0.34). The 16+ logit/LPM show the same direction (Hispanic log-odds −1.12 → −0.29) but are underpowered. Hypothesis: much of the observed race gap in education attainment is associated with differences in measured academic characteristics (cognitive ability and class standing), so considering academic characteristics substantially attenuates the race effects, whereas the family-income association is robust to those controls. Because the academic characteristics (1981) are measured after the 1979 grade outcome, these coefficient shifts are association/attenuation, not causal mediation; no time-ordered causal claim is made."

WORKFLOW SUMMARY
"Loaded data/nls_raw.csv (12,686 × 61). Verified by full column audit + keyword search that no BA/degree column exists; the only education-attainment variable is highest grade completed in 1979 (two '95' special-code rows set to missing). Constructed: race dummies (Black, Hispanic vs non-Black/non-Hispanic ref); log1p(1979 family income); mother's/father's 1979 grade; ASVAB composite = mean of the four 1981 sections, treated as 500/100 standard scores; class-rank percentile = 1 − rank/class size (2 rank>size observations clipped to 0). SES restricted to pre-1979/1979 measures; 1985/1990/1996 wealth and 1985/1989 income excluded as predictors. Complete-case modeling (n=3,717). Estimated OLS on continuous grade and logit + linear probability on the 16+ binary, each in a baseline (race + SES) and an augmented (+ academic) specification; compared coefficients before/after to quantify attenuation. Code: build_analysis.py; full output: analysis_output.txt."
